title: Quantum synchronization of spin-1 system: Enhanced synchronization due to additive Lindblad operators
authors: Tran Duong Anh-Tai, S. Zhong, X. Molenda, A. M. Marino, D. Blume
abstract: We experimentally investigate quantum synchronization for one of the simplest possible quantum systems, namely an externally driven few-level system with equally spaced energy levels effectively acting as a spin-1 system. Coupling to excited auxiliary states, we realize additive effective Lindblad operators that are associated with non-conventional dissipative pathways, which are shown to enhance, in certain parameter regimes, quantum synchronization. The experimental set-up, which utilizes cold $^{87}$Rb atoms in a MOT, and associated synchronization extraction protocol are benchmarked carefully through dedicated simulations. Convincing agreement is found between experiment and simulations. The dissipation engineering approach established in our work can be readily extended to systems with more energy levels, such as effective spin-$3/2$ or spin-$2$ systems, and has implications for quantum synchronization studies in higher-spin systems as well as for a wide range of quantum science studies and technology applications.
summary: This research experimentally investigates quantum synchronization in a spin-1 system realized with cold $^{87}	ext{Rb}$ atoms. By engineering the dissipation using additive Lindblad operators, the authors demonstrate that these non-conventional decay pathways can significantly enhance the observed quantum synchronization. The work validates the theoretical model against precise measurements, suggesting a general technique for controlling quantum dynamics in higher-spin systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates quantum synchronization in a spin-1 system, focusing on how engineered dissipative pathways can enhance this collective quantum behavior.
main_result: The implementation of additive Lindblad operators, achieved through dissipation engineering, was shown to enhance quantum synchronization in certain parameter regimes, with experimental results showing convincing agreement with simulations.
method: The study uses a hybrid approach combining theoretical derivation (effective spin-1 master equation from a full 6-state Hamiltonian) with experimental realization using cold atoms.
model_or_system: The system is an externally driven few-level system, effectively modeled as a spin-1 system, realized using cold $^{87}	ext{Rb}$ atoms in a Magneto-Optical Trap (MOT). The dynamics are governed by an effective Lindbladian incorporating non-conventional dissipative pathways.
key_observables: Quantum synchronization measure $S_q(t, z)$, normalized probe beam intensity $I_{	ext{norm}}^{\pi}(t)$, and the effective spin-1 master equation.
important_parameters: Rabi coupling strengths ($\Omega$), decay rates ($\Gamma$), magnetic field strength ($B$), and the relative phase ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on second-order time-dependent perturbation theory, and the MOT is treated as a 1D medium with low atomic density.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the laser beam geometry, energy level diagrams, Husimi-Q functions, and quantitative comparisons of the synchronization measure $S_q$ between the effective spin-1 model and the full 6-state model, alongside time evolution of probe intensity.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical setup and deriving the effective spin-1 model from the full 6-state Hamiltonian, demonstrating the enhancement of synchronization due to engineered dissipation, and finally validating these findings by comparing simulation results against experimental measurements of probe intensity.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete experimental platform (cold atoms) to study non-trivial open quantum system dynamics, specifically demonstrating how controlling dissipation (dissipation engineering) can actively enhance quantum coherence measures like synchronization.
